title: Your Text to VOYAGER 1 Would Take a Whole DAY 🛰️
description:
Text Voyager 1 right now, and your message wouldn't arrive until tomorrow. It's not ignoring you: even light takes that long. Your text would zip past the Moon in about a second and Pluto in about five hours, but it needs a whole day to reach Voyager 1. And its reply? Another whole day. Beep. It took Voyager 49 years to get this far, and the nearest star is about 1,500 times farther.
Would you wait for the reply? Yes or no?

The science: on 18 November 2026, at 10:16 UTC (15:46 IST), NASA's Voyager 1 became the first human-made object one light-day from Earth: about 25.9 billion km (16.1 billion miles, 173 AU), the distance light travels in 24 hours. It launched on 5 September 1977, flew past Jupiter (1979) and Saturn (1980), and left the Sun's bubble, the heliosphere, in 2012. Radio travels at the speed of light, so a command now takes about a day to reach it, and its answer about a day to come back. Light reaches the Moon in about 1.3 seconds and Pluto, about 35 times farther from us than the Sun, in about five hours. The nearest star, Proxima Centauri, is about 4.2 light-years away: roughly 1,550 light-days. At Voyager's speed (about 17 km a second) that trip would take about 75,000 years, and Voyager isn't even heading that way. (Its chat status says last seen 1977, and its reply says beep: those two are jokes. It answers in data.)
